title: Start a PR on the metered API
say: Start the PR for card 412 with DeepSeek.

steps.t: Wake word, VAD, transcription as above.
An action: the fast lane never answers it. It says 'On it.' and hands off your verbatim words.
Your words are typed into the PA chat through termhub. Claude Code calls card 412 (allowed) and then factory_start {card: 412, runtime: api, model: azure/deepseek-v4-pro, delivery: pr}.

factory_start is on no allow list: Claude Code shows a permission prompt. Jarvis asks "Start a factory job for card 412 on the API with azure/deepseek-v4-pro, opening a PR for review. Shall I?" and you say yes (or press Approve on the dashboard).

dispatch.start composes the brief from the card (PA_COMPOSE_MODEL), writes a flow file, and runs `uv run factory job submit --json --runtime api --model dev=azure/deepseek-v4-pro --delivery pr` on the factory machine.
On the work stack the factory is on the same machine: the command goes to factory serve (POST 127.0.0.1:7330/api/cli). The PA spawns uv run factory only when nothing is listening.
The factory answers one JSON object with the job id; the PA records the run.

Solo pipeline: one dev agent, one independent review (azure/Kimi-K2.7-Code, one fix round only on a high or blocking finding, or on test slop or a score under 0.7; medium and low do not spend a round), the tech_writer commits its context update on the story branch, then gates, a PR, and the CI watch (up to 3 CI-fix cycles; a held worktree gets a sibling checkout).
OpenHands runs the dev step; LiteLLM calls the DeepSeek-V4-Pro deployment on Azure.
Metered: the spend shows in the job's cost_usd.
Branch pushed, ready PR opened, checks watched; delivered_pr, never merged.

The factory pass (every 5 s while the job moves) stores `job list` in factory_board; its trigger puts the change on the live feed, so the Factory page redraws at once; it and the chat's factory_job show state, PR and cost; a notification tells you.

acceptance.outcome: A ready PR is opened on the repo through the metered DeepSeek API runtime, never merged.

hops.what: tool call (card, factory_start) excluding model time

hops.unbounded: bound by the model and the repo gates; no latency target
bound by CI; at most 3 CI-fix cycles

hops.what: state change to the board redraw

cost.basis: job cost_usd: dev on azure/deepseek-v4-pro, the other steps on the azure routes (pm and sm DeepSeek-V4-Flash, reviewer and tech_writer Kimi-K2.7-Code); the PA's compose call is outside it

rubric.check: The PR is open and ready for review.
CI is green on the PR head.
An independent code review finds no blocker.
The diff stays inside what the card asked for.

title: Continue a PR on the subscription
say: Fix the review comments on PR 12.

steps.t: Hand-off to the PA chat.
Calls factory_continue {pr: 12, repo}: runtime defaults to claude_session because you did not ask for the API. You approve the prompt.

The brief says "commit onto PR #12's branch, open no new pull request" and leaves the review comments to the factory. `job submit --pr 12 --runtime claude_session` reads the PR and its unresolved review threads in one GraphQL call, with `claude auth status` alongside, and appends the threads to the brief. job submit --pr is in the contract; a factory that does not know --pr refuses in its parser and the job fails saying so, never resent as fresh work.
The factory checks `claude auth status` is a claude.ai login, then starts `claude -p --output-format stream-json` in a termhub session with API-key variables removed.

The session lives in the factory machine's termhub (on the work stack, the Windows termhub); its URL is in runs[].session, so you can open it live from the Factory page, where the job's card says "continues PR #12" (the job's `base`).
Billed to the subscription: cost_usd 0, the API-price equivalent goes to subscription_equiv_usd.
The fix is pushed fast-forward to the same PR; the CI watch restarts on the new head.

acceptance.outcome: The existing PR is updated in place (fast-forward push) so its review comments are resolved, on the subscription.

hops.unbounded: bound by the model; no latency target

hops.what: CI watch on the new head to green
hops.unbounded: bound by CI; at most 3 CI-fix cycles

hops.what: state change to the board redraw

cost.basis: the agent runs on the claude.ai subscription (subscription_equiv_usd recorded, not billed); the factory's planning steps (pm, sm) run metered on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and its docs step (tech_writer) on Kimi-K2.7-Code, about $0.01-0.03 a job (D26)

rubric.check: The same PR is updated; no new PR is opened and nothing is merged.
CI is green on the new head.
A code review finds no blocker and each comment is addressed or answered.
The diff stays inside the review comments.

title: A research report
say: Research how our deploy pipeline handles rollbacks and write it up.

steps.t: You asked for research explicitly, so the chat calls factory_start {kind: research, ask: your words}; you approve the prompt.
A research job delivers none; its ask is your own words (no composing model).
job submit --kind research returns an id like app:r0007.
factory serve starts a detached worker (a wake within 1 s of submit; at most 2 at a time).
One Claude Code conversation (claude_session by default from the chat) writes report.md; 5400 s cap.
state/jobs/r0007-<slug>/report.md is kept by the factory.
The poll sees it done; factory_job returns the report excerpt and the Factory page renders the report as a parsed tree (no HTML sink).

acceptance.outcome: A report.md answers the question you asked, with its sources cited, delivered by a research job that opens no PR.

hops.unbounded: bound by the model; 5400 s cap

hops.what: state change to the board redraw

cost.basis: the agent runs on the claude.ai subscription (subscription_equiv_usd recorded, not billed); the factory's planning steps (pm, sm) run metered on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and its docs step (tech_writer) on Kimi-K2.7-Code, about $0.01-0.03 a job (D26)

rubric.check: Every claim carries a source, and each source was opened and checked.
No claim is unsupported by its source.
The report answers the question asked, not an adjacent one.
